papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. papers.summary: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. papers.summary: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. papers.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. papers.summary: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. papers.summary: Facial deepfake detectors are usually trained on blending fakes, where a generated face is pasted back into a real frame.
